nodes.statement_short: Split on whether the monomial degree $r$ is at most $k_m$: in one case use $|1-\Upsilon(\alpha(1))^{k_m-\kappa}| \le |\tilde\pi^{\tau(m)+1}|$, in the other the weight decay, then combine into an operator-norm bound.

nodes.name: Write the difference on a monomial
nodes.statement: Write \begin{equation} \left( [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} - [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa \right) (e_{u_1} e_{u_2} \cdots e_{u_r} ) = \left( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{k_m - r} - \Upsilon( \alpha_{ a d(\bar t)}(1))^{\kappa - r} \right) ( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(\tilde \pi^{w(u_1)} x^{u_1} ))) \cdots ( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(\tilde \pi^{w(u_r)} x^{u_r} ))). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Express the difference of the two operators on $e_{u_1}\cdots e_{u_r}$ as a product with a single differing factor.

nodes.name: Case $r \le k_m$
nodes.statement: If $r \leq k_m$, then the first factor on the right may itself be factored into \[ -\Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{\kappa - r} (1 - (\Upsilon(\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{k_m - \kappa}). \] Writing $\kappa = k_m + p^{\tau(m)} \sigma_m$ (with $\tau(m) \rightarrow \infty$ and $\sigma_m \in \bb Z_p$) then \[ | 1 - (\Upsilon(\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(1))^{k_m - \kappa} | \leq | \tilde \pi^{\tau(m) + 1} | \] as in the proof of \cite[Lemma 2.2]{MR3249829}, and using the estimate (\ref{E: upsilon estimate}).
nodes.statement_short: Factor out $\Upsilon(\alpha(1))^{\kappa-r}$ and bound $|1-\Upsilon(\alpha(1))^{k_m-\kappa}|$ by $|\tilde\pi^{\tau(m)+1}|$.

nodes.name: Case $r > k_m$
nodes.statement: If $r > k_m$ then (\ref{E: double star}) becomes \begin{align*} \left( [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} - [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa \right) (e_{\b u} ) = -[\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa e_{\b u} = - \Upsilon( \alpha_{ a d(\bar t)}(1))^{\kappa - r} ( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(\tilde \pi^{w(u_1)} x^{u_1} ))) \cdots ( \Upsilon( \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}(\tilde \pi^{w(u_r)} x^{u_r} ))) \end{align*} so that focussing on the $r$ rightmost factors, \[ \left| \left( [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} - [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa \right) e_{\b u} \right| \leq |\tilde \pi|^{\frac{p^{a d(\bar t) - 1} - 1}{p-1} \frac{1}{p^{a d(\bar t) - 1}} w(\b u)} \] coming from (\ref{E: upsilon estimate}). But $w(\b u) \geq r w_0 > k_m w_0$ (where $w_0 := \min \{ w(\b u) \mid \b u \in M(f) \setminus \{0\} \}$).
nodes.statement_short: Here the truncated map vanishes, so the difference is bounded by the weight decay $|\tilde\pi|^{\cdots w(\b u)}$ with $w(\b u) > k_m w_0$.

nodes.name: Combine into an operator norm bound and pass to the limit
nodes.statement: In terms of the operator norm, \[ \| [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa - [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} \| \leq | \tilde \pi |^{\min \left\{ \tau(m) + 1, \frac{p^{a d(\bar t) -1} - 1}{p-1} \frac{1}{p^{a d(\bar t) -1}} k_m w_0 \right\} }. \] As $k_m$ and $\tau(m)$ both tend to infinity as $m$ grows, we see that $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)} ]_{(\kappa; m)} = [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_\kappa$.
nodes.statement_short: Take the minimum of the two bounds; both exponents tend to infinity, giving the operator-norm convergence.

nodes.name: Limit of the truncated dual Frobenius maps
nodes.statement: In an altogether similar manner, we have by Lemma \ref{L: better conv}, for $u \not= 0$, $\alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u})$ belongs to $\c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m})$, and (recalling (\ref{E: an estimate})) \[ | \alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u}) | \leq | \tilde \pi |^{(p-1) w(u)}. \] Also $\alpha_m^*(1) = 1 + \eta^*(\lambda)$ with $\eta^*(\lambda) \in \c O_{0, p^m}$ and $|\eta^*(\lambda)| \leq |\tilde \pi|$. With these observations, an entirely similar argument shows $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* ]_{(\kappa; m)} = [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_\kappa$ as maps from $\c S_0^*(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}}) \rightarrow \c S_0^*(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}}) $.
nodes.statement_short: The same argument, using the dual estimates, gives $\lim_m [\alpha^*_{ad(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa;m)} = [\alpha^*_{ad(\bar t)}]_\kappa$.
assumptions: we have by Lemma \ref{L: better conv}, for $u \not= 0$, $\alpha_m^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u})$ belongs to $\c C_0^*(\c O_{0, p^m})$
conclusions: $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* ]_{(\kappa; m)} = [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_\kappa$ as maps from $\c S_0^*(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}}) \rightarrow \c S_0^*(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}}) $.

nodes.name: The truncated operators $\beta_{(\kappa;m),\bar t}$ and $\beta^*_{(\kappa;m),\bar t}$
nodes.statement: Define \begin{align*} \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} &:= \psi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)} \circ [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} \\ \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* &:= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \circ [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} \circ \Phi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)}. \end{align*} As $\psi_\lambda$ and $\Phi_\lambda$ are bounded maps, it follows that as operators on $\c S_0(\c O_0)$ and $\c S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$, respectively, \begin{align} \lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} &= \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} \\ \lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* &= \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^*. \notag \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Truncated analogues of $\beta$ and $\beta^*$, which converge to them since $\psi_\lambda$ and $\Phi_\lambda$ are bounded.

nodes.name: Lemma (adjointness of $\beta_{(\kappa;m),\bar t}$ and $\beta^*_{(\kappa;m),\bar t}$)
nodes.statement: For $\xi \in \c S_0^{(k_m)}(\c O_0)$ and $\xi^* \in \c S_0^{*(k_m)}(\c O_0^*)$, \begin{equation} \langle \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} \xi, \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} = \langle \xi, \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* \xi^* \rangle_{k_m}. \end{equation}
conclusions: \langle \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} \xi, \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} = \langle \xi, \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* \xi^* \rangle_{k_m}

nodes.name: Proof of the adjointness of the truncated operators
nodes.statement: With $\xi \in \c S_0^{(k_m)}(\c O_0)$ and $\xi^* \in \c S_0^{*(k_m)}(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}})$, we may rewrite (\ref{E: dual sym}) as \begin{equation} ( [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa, m)} \xi, \xi^*)_{k_m} = (\xi, [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} \xi^*)_{k_m}. \end{equation} Next, by linearity we only need consider $\xi = \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u}$ and $\xi^* = \lambda^{-\sigma} e_{\b v}^*$ where $\gamma, \sigma \in M(\Gamma)$ and $\b u, \b v \in S(M)$. We may write \[ (e_{\b u}, [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} e_{\b v}^*)_{k_m} = \sum_{\tau \in M(\Gamma)} C(\tau) \lambda^\tau. \] Next, observe that \[ \langle \psi_\lambda \xi, \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} = \langle \xi, \Phi_\lambda \xi^* \rangle_{k_m}. \] Hence, in the case $\xi = \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u}$ and $\xi^* = \lambda^{-\sigma} e_{\b v}^*$, \begin{align*} \langle \beta_{(\kappa; m)} \xi, \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} &= \langle [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} \xi, \Phi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)} \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} \\ &= \text{constant term of } \left[ \lambda^{\gamma - q_{\bar t} \sigma} ([\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} e_{\b u}, e_{\b v}^*)_{k_m} \right] \\ &= \text{constant of } \left[ \lambda^{\gamma - q_{\bar t} \sigma} ( e_{\b u}, [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} e_{\b v}^*)_{k_m} \right] \qquad \text{ by (\ref{E: rewrite duality}}) \\ &= \text{constant of } \left[ \lambda^{\gamma - q_{\bar t} \sigma} \sum_{\tau \in M(\Gamma)} C(\tau) \lambda^{\tau} \right] \\ &= \begin{cases} C(q_{\bar t} \sigma - \gamma) & \text{if } q_{\bar t} \sigma - \gamma \in M(\Gamma) \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \end{align*} In the other direction, again setting $\xi = \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u}$ and $\xi^* = \lambda^{-\sigma} e_{\b v}^*$, \begin{align*} \langle \xi, \beta_{(\kappa; m)}^* \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} &= \text{constant term of } \left[ \lambda^\gamma \cdot \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)}\left( \lambda^{-q_{\bar t} \sigma} (e_{\b u}, [\alpha_{a d(\bar t}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} e_{\b v}^*)_{k_m} ) \right) \right] \\ &= \text{constant of } \left[ \lambda^\gamma \cdot \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)}\left( \sum_{\tau \in M(\Gamma)} C(\tau) \lambda^{-(q_{\bar t} \sigma - \tau)} \right) \right] \\ &= \text{constant of } \left[ \lambda^\gamma \cdot \sum_{\substack{\tau \in M(\Gamma) \text{ s.t.} \\ q_{\bar t} \sigma - \tau \in M(\Gamma)}} C(\tau) \lambda^{-(q_{\bar t} \sigma - \tau)} \right] \\ &= \begin{cases} C(q_{\bar t} \sigma - \gamma) & \text{if } q_{\bar t} \sigma - \gamma \in M(\Gamma) \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to monomials $\xi=\lambda^\gamma e_{\b u}$, $\xi^*=\lambda^{-\sigma}e^*_{\b v}$ and compute both sides to the same value $C(q_{\bar t}\sigma-\gamma)$.

nodes.name: Rewrite the symmetric-power duality for truncated maps
nodes.statement: With $\xi \in \c S_0^{(k_m)}(\c O_0)$ and $\xi^* \in \c S_0^{*(k_m)}(\c O_{0, q_{\bar t}})$, we may rewrite (\ref{E: dual sym}) as \begin{equation} ( [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa, m)} \xi, \xi^*)_{k_m} = (\xi, [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} \xi^*)_{k_m}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Transport the finite symmetric-power adjointness to the truncated operators.

nodes.name: Reduce to monomials and record the expansion
nodes.statement: Next, by linearity we only need consider $\xi = \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u}$ and $\xi^* = \lambda^{-\sigma} e_{\b v}^*$ where $\gamma, \sigma \in M(\Gamma)$ and $\b u, \b v \in S(M)$. We may write \[ (e_{\b u}, [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} e_{\b v}^*)_{k_m} = \sum_{\tau \in M(\Gamma)} C(\tau) \lambda^\tau. \] Next, observe that \[ \langle \psi_\lambda \xi, \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} = \langle \xi, \Phi_\lambda \xi^* \rangle_{k_m}. \]
nodes.statement_short: By linearity it suffices to treat monomials, and $\psi_\lambda$ is adjoint to $\Phi_\lambda$.

nodes.name: Compute $\langle \beta_{(\kappa;m)}\xi, \xi^* \rangle_{k_m}$
nodes.statement: Hence, in the case $\xi = \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u}$ and $\xi^* = \lambda^{-\sigma} e_{\b v}^*$, \begin{align*} \langle \beta_{(\kappa; m)} \xi, \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} &= \langle [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} \xi, \Phi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)} \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} \\ &= \text{constant term of } \left[ \lambda^{\gamma - q_{\bar t} \sigma} ([\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}]_{(\kappa; m)} e_{\b u}, e_{\b v}^*)_{k_m} \right] \\ &= \text{constant of } \left[ \lambda^{\gamma - q_{\bar t} \sigma} ( e_{\b u}, [\alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} e_{\b v}^*)_{k_m} \right] \qquad \text{ by (\ref{E: rewrite duality}}) \\ &= \text{constant of } \left[ \lambda^{\gamma - q_{\bar t} \sigma} \sum_{\tau \in M(\Gamma)} C(\tau) \lambda^{\tau} \right] \\ &= \begin{cases} C(q_{\bar t} \sigma - \gamma) & \text{if } q_{\bar t} \sigma - \gamma \in M(\Gamma) \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Extracting the constant term gives $C(q_{\bar t}\sigma-\gamma)$ when that index lies in $M(\Gamma)$, else $0$.

nodes.name: Compute the other side and match
nodes.statement: In the other direction, again setting $\xi = \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u}$ and $\xi^* = \lambda^{-\sigma} e_{\b v}^*$, \begin{align*} \langle \xi, \beta_{(\kappa; m)}^* \xi^* \rangle_{k_m} &= \text{constant term of } \left[ \lambda^\gamma \cdot \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)}\left( \lambda^{-q_{\bar t} \sigma} (e_{\b u}, [\alpha_{a d(\bar t}^*]_{(\kappa; m)} e_{\b v}^*)_{k_m} ) \right) \right] \\ &= \text{constant of } \left[ \lambda^\gamma \cdot \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)}\left( \sum_{\tau \in M(\Gamma)} C(\tau) \lambda^{-(q_{\bar t} \sigma - \tau)} \right) \right] \\ &= \text{constant of } \left[ \lambda^\gamma \cdot \sum_{\substack{\tau \in M(\Gamma) \text{ s.t.} \\ q_{\bar t} \sigma - \tau \in M(\Gamma)}} C(\tau) \lambda^{-(q_{\bar t} \sigma - \tau)} \right] \\ &= \begin{cases} C(q_{\bar t} \sigma - \gamma) & \text{if } q_{\bar t} \sigma - \gamma \in M(\Gamma) \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The same computation for $\langle \xi, \beta^*_{(\kappa;m)}\xi^* \rangle_{k_m}$ produces the identical value, proving adjointness.

nodes.name: Convergence of the Fredholm determinants
nodes.statement: Observe that $\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ and $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}$ are completely continuous operators on the $p$-adic Banach $R$-algebra $\c S_0(\c O_0)$ (viewed as $R$-algebra) with orthonormal basis $\{ \tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u} \mid \gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M) \}$. Let $\c T_0(R) \ \text{be} \ \c S_0(\c O_0)$ viewed in this way as $R$-algebra. Similarly, write $\c T_0^*(R)$ for the $b(I)$-space (over $R$) in Serre's terminology with ``basis'' $I := \{ \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^* \mid \gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M) \}$ with coefficients in $R$. Again, $\c T_0^*(R)$ is just $\c S_0^*(\c O_0^*)$ viewed over $R$. Then \[ \lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T) = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T). \]
nodes.statement_short: On the Banach algebra $\c T_0(R)$, $det(1-\beta_{(\kappa;m),\bar t}T) \to det(1-\beta_{\kappa,\bar t}T)$.
assumptions: Observe that $\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ and $\beta_{\kappa, \bar t}$ are completely continuous operators on the $p$-adic Banach $R$-algebra $\c S_0(\c O_0)$ (viewed as $R$-algebra) with orthonormal basis $\{ \tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^\gamma e_{\b u} \mid \gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M) \}$.
conclusions: \lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T) = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T)

nodes.name: Proof of the equality of Fredholm determinants
nodes.statement: Similarly, $\beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ is a continuous $R$-linear endomorphism of $\c T_0^*(R)$ to itself. We may consider a matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ with entries in $R$ defined by \[ \beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}( \tilde \pi^{-w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^*) = \sum \f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}_{(\delta, \b v), (\gamma, \b u)} \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\delta)} \lambda^{-\delta} e_{\b v}^*. \] Using the matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$, we define in the usual way the Fredholm determinant $det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* T) = \sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^*) T^j$ where $C_0 = 1$ and $C_j$ is the series of all principal $j \times j$ subdeterminants of the matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$. The $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_{k_m}$-adjointness of $\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ and $\beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ implies $C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}) = C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^*)$, so that \[ det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* T) = det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T). \] The uniform convergence $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} \f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t} =: \f B^*_{\kappa, \bar t}$ over the entries implies that the series $\sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\f B_{\kappa, \bar t}^*) T^j$ is well-defined, and is the coefficient-wise limit of $det(1 - \f B^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T)$ as $m \rightarrow \infty$. If we then define \[ det(1 - \beta^*_{\kappa, \bar t} T) := \sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\f B_{\kappa, \bar t}^*) T^j, \]
nodes.statement_short: Build the dual matrix, use $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{k_m}$-adjointness to equate the subdeterminants $C_j$, then pass to the limit to define $det(1-\beta^*_{\kappa,\bar t}T)$.

nodes.name: Introduce the dual matrix and its Fredholm determinant
nodes.statement: Similarly, $\beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ is a continuous $R$-linear endomorphism of $\c T_0^*(R)$ to itself. We may consider a matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ with entries in $R$ defined by \[ \beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}( \tilde \pi^{-w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^*) = \sum \f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}_{(\delta, \b v), (\gamma, \b u)} \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\delta)} \lambda^{-\delta} e_{\b v}^*. \] Using the matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$, we define in the usual way the Fredholm determinant $det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* T) = \sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^*) T^j$ where $C_0 = 1$ and $C_j$ is the series of all principal $j \times j$ subdeterminants of the matrix $\f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t}$.
nodes.statement_short: Represent $\beta^*_{(\kappa;m),\bar t}$ by a matrix over $R$ and form $det(1-\beta^*_{(\kappa;m),\bar t}T)$ from its principal minors.

nodes.name: Adjointness equates the coefficients $C_j$
nodes.statement: The $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_{k_m}$-adjointness of $\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ and $\beta^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}$ implies $C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}) = C_j(\beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^*)$, so that \[ det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t}^* T) = det(1 - \beta_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T). \]
nodes.statement_short: Adjointness forces $C_j(\beta_{(\kappa;m)}) = C_j(\beta^*_{(\kappa;m)})$, so the truncated determinants agree.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit to define $det(1-\beta^*_{\kappa,\bar t}T)$
nodes.statement: The uniform convergence $\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} \f B^{*(\kappa; m), \bar t} =: \f B^*_{\kappa, \bar t}$ over the entries implies that the series $\sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\f B_{\kappa, \bar t}^*) T^j$ is well-defined, and is the coefficient-wise limit of $det(1 - \f B^*_{(\kappa; m), \bar t} T)$ as $m \rightarrow \infty$. If we then define \[ det(1 - \beta^*_{\kappa, \bar t} T) := \sum_{j \geq 0} (-1)^{j+1} C_j(\f B_{\kappa, \bar t}^*) T^j, \]
nodes.statement_short: Entrywise uniform convergence of the matrices makes the limiting series well defined, which we take as the dual Fredholm determinant.

nodes.name: Theorem (equality of the Fredholm determinants)
nodes.statement: $det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T) = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^* T)$, and thus from (\ref{E: A}), \begin{equation} L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}} = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^* T)^{\delta_{q_{\bar t}}^{s}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The primal and dual Fredholm determinants agree, so $L^{(0)}$ is also computed by the dual operator.
conclusions: $det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t} T) = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^* T)$
L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}} = det(1 - \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^* T)^{\delta_{q_{\bar t}}^{s}}

nodes.name: The generic family $H(\Lambda,\lambda,x)$
nodes.statement: We now replace every coefficient of $G$ (w.r.t the variables $x$ and $\lambda$) with a new variable $\Lambda$: set $ \b f(\Lambda,x)=\sum_{u \in Supp(f)} \Lambda_u x^u \ \text{and} \ \c P(\Lambda, \lambda. x) = \sum_{(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)} \Lambda_{\gamma, v} \lambda^\gamma x^v$ and \[ H(\Lambda, \lambda, x) := \b f(\Lambda,x) + \c P(\Lambda, \lambda. x) . \]
nodes.statement_short: Replace all coefficients of $G$ in $x$ and $\lambda$ by independent variables $\Lambda$ to obtain $H = \b f(\Lambda,x)+\c P(\Lambda,\lambda,x)$.

nodes.name: $\Delta_\infty(H)$, $Cone(H)$ and $M(H)$
nodes.statement: As before, let $\Delta_{\infty}(H)$ denote the Newton polytope at infinity in $\bb R^{s+n}$ of $H$ (in $\lambda$ and $x$ variables). Let $Cone(H)$ be the cone in $\bb R^{s+n}$ over $\Delta_{\infty}(H)$ and $M(H) = Cone(H) \cap \bb Z^{s+n}$ be the relevant monoid.

nodes.name: The total weight is dominated by $w_H$
nodes.statement: Clearly $M(H) \subset M(\Gamma) \times M(f)$. By our hypothesis that the $x$-support of $P$ is contained in $\Delta_{\infty}(f)$ we have the polyhedral weight function on this polytope $w_H$ dominates the total weight $w_{\text{tot}} := w_{\Gamma} + w_f$ relative to the polyhedron $\Gamma \times \Delta_{\infty}$; more precisely \[ w_{\text{tot}}(\gamma, u) \leq w_H(\gamma, u) \] for all $(\gamma, u) \in M(H)$.
nodes.statement_short: Under the support hypothesis on $P$, $w_{tot} = w_\Gamma + w_f \le w_H$ on $M(H)$.
assumptions: By our hypothesis that the $x$-support of $P$ is contained in $\Delta_{\infty}(f)$
conclusions: w_{\text{tot}}(\gamma, u) \leq w_H(\gamma, u)

nodes.name: The rings $\c K$ and $\c K_0$
nodes.statement: We define $\c K := R[[\Lambda]]$ and \[ \c K_0 := \{ \xi \in \sum_{v \in \bb Z_{\geq 0}^t} \xi_v \Lambda^v \in \c K \mid \xi_v \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } v \rightarrow \infty \}, \] where $t$ is the cardinality of $\{ Supp(f) \} \cup \{ Supp(P) \}$. We endow both spaces with the sup norm on coefficients.

nodes.name: The spaces $\c W(\c K_0)$, $\c W_0(\c K_0)$, $\c D(\c W(\c K_0))$, $\c D_0(\c W_0(\c K_0))$
nodes.statement: Define the spaces \begin{align*} \c W(\c K_0) &:= \{ \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)} \xi_\gamma(\Lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} \mid \xi_\gamma(\Lambda) \in \c K_0 \} \\ \c W_0(\c K_0) &:= \{ \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma)} \xi_\gamma(\Lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} \mid \xi_\gamma(\Lambda) \in \c K_0, \xi_\gamma(\Lambda) \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } \gamma \rightarrow \infty \}. \end{align*} Similarly, we define as well \begin{align*} \c D( \c W(\c K_0)) &:= \{ \sum_{(\gamma, u) \in M(\Gamma) \times M(f) } \xi_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma) - w(u)} \lambda^{-\gamma} x^{-u} \mid \xi_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) \in \c K_0 \} \\ \c D_0( \c W_0( \c K_0) ) &:= \{ \sum_{(\gamma, u) \in M(\Gamma) \times M(f) } \xi_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma) - w(u)} \lambda^{-\gamma} x^{-u} \mid \xi_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) \in \c K_0, \sup_{\gamma} | \xi_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda)| \rightarrow 0 \text{ as } u \rightarrow \infty \}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Dual-type spaces of $\lambda^{-\gamma}$ (and $x^{-u}$) series with coefficients in $\c K_0$, with and without decay.

nodes.name: The spaces $\c S_0^*(\c W(\c K_0))$ and $\c S_0^*(\c W_0(\c K_0))$
nodes.statement: We proceed similar to our work above. We define a $\c K_0$-module \[ \c S^*_0(\c W(\c K_0)) := \{ \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M)} A_{\gamma, \b u}(\Lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_{\b u}^* \mid A_{\gamma, \b u} \in \c K_0 \}. \] and a $\c W_0(\c K_0)$-algebra \[ \c S^*_0(\c W_0(\c K_0)) := \{ \sum_{\gamma \in M(\Gamma), \b u \in S(M)} \xi^*_{ \b u}(\Lambda, \lambda) e_{\b u}^* \mid \xi^*_{ \b u}(\Lambda, \lambda) \in \c W_0(K_0) \}. \] As before define an embedding $\Upsilon: \c D(\c W(\c K_0))) \hookrightarrow \c S^*_0(\c W(\c K_0))$ by $\tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u} \mapsto e_u^*$ for $u \in M \setminus \{0\}$ and $\Upsilon(1) := 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Infinite symmetric power versions of the $\c W$-spaces, with the embedding $\Upsilon$ defined as before.

nodes.name: Relative Frobenius $F(\Lambda,\lambda,x)$, $F_m$ and $\alpha_m^*(\Lambda,\lambda)$
nodes.statement: We define a relative Frobenius map as follows. First, set \begin{align*} F(\Lambda, \lambda, x) &:= \prod_{u \in Supp(f)} \theta(\Lambda_u x^u) \cdot \prod_{(\gamma, v) \in Supp(P)} \theta( \Lambda_{\gamma, v} \lambda^\gamma x^v) \\ F_m(\Lambda, \lambda, x) &:= \prod_{i=0}^{m-1} F(\Lambda^{p^i}, \lambda^{p^i}, x^{p^i}), \end{align*} and note that, similar to before, \[ F_m(\Lambda, \lambda, x) = \sum_{(\gamma, u) \in M(H)} \c F^m_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) \lambda^{\gamma} x^u \] with $\c F^m_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda)= B_{\gamma,u}(\Lambda) \tilde{\pi}^{w_{tot}(\gamma,u)/p^{m-1}} = \b B_{\gamma,u}(\Lambda) \tilde{\pi}^{w_H(\gamma,u)/p^{m-1}}$. It follows that, if we set (as before) \[ \alpha_m^*(\Lambda, \lambda) := \text{pr}_{M(f)} \circ F_m(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \circ \Phi_x^m, \]
nodes.statement_short: Splitting-function product in the generic coefficients $\Lambda$, its Frobenius iterate, and the associated dual operator.

nodes.name: Mapping property of $\alpha^*_{m,\Lambda}$
nodes.statement: then an argument similar to Lemma \ref{L: better conv} shows \[ \alpha_{m, \Lambda}^*: \c D_0(\c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0)) \rightarrow \c D_0(\c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0)), \] where $\c W_{0, p^m}$ is defined by replacing $\tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma}$ with $\tilde \pi^{w_{p^m \Gamma}}$ in the definition of $\c W_0$. Furthermore, \[ \alpha_{m, \Lambda}^*(\tilde \pi^{-w(v)} x^{-v}) = \sum_{u \in M(f)} C_{u, v}(\Lambda, \gamma) \tilde \pi^{-w(u)} x^{-u} \] with $C_{u, v}(\Lambda, \lambda) \in \c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0)$ and $C_{u, v}(\Lambda, \lambda) \rightarrow 0$ as $w(u) \rightarrow \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: The relative dual Frobenius preserves $\c D_0(\c W_{0,p^m}(\c K_0))$ with coefficients tending to $0$.
assumptions: an argument similar to Lemma \ref{L: better conv} shows
conclusions: \alpha_{m, \Lambda}^*: \c D_0(\c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0)) \rightarrow \c D_0(\c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0))
with $C_{u, v}(\Lambda, \lambda) \in \c W_{0, p^m}(\c K_0)$ and $C_{u, v}(\Lambda, \lambda) \rightarrow 0$ as $w(u) \rightarrow \infty$.

nodes.name: $\beta^*_{\kappa,\bar t,\Lambda}$ is an endomorphism over $\c K_0$
nodes.statement: By an argument similar to Lemma \ref{L: beta is endo}, the map \[ \beta_{\kappa, \bar t, \Lambda}^*: \c S^*_0(\c W(\c K_0)) \rightarrow \c S^*_0(\c W(\c K_0)) \] defined by \[ \beta_{\kappa, \bar t, \Lambda}^* := \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \circ [ \alpha_{a d(\bar t)}^* ]_\kappa \circ \Phi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)}. \] is an endomorphism over $\c K_0$.
assumptions: By an argument similar to Lemma \ref{L: beta is endo}
conclusions: \beta_{\kappa, \bar t, \Lambda}^*: \c S^*_0(\c W(\c K_0)) \rightarrow \c S^*_0(\c W(\c K_0))

nodes.name: The symmetric monoids $M_0$ and the projection $\text{pr}_0$
nodes.statement: Set $M_0(\Gamma) = M(\Gamma) \cap (- M(\Gamma)), M_0(f) = M(f) \cap (- M(f)), \ \text{and} \ M_0(H) = M(H) \cap (-M(H))$. Define the projection map \[ \text{pr}_0: \quad \sum_{\gamma \in \bb Z^s, u \in \bb Z^n} C(\gamma, u) \lambda^\gamma x^u \longmapsto \sum_{\gamma \in M_0(\Gamma), u \in M_0(f)} C(\gamma, u) \lambda^\gamma x^u. \]

nodes.name: The coefficients $J_{\gamma,u}(\Lambda)$ and $\tilde J_{\gamma,u}(\Lambda)$
nodes.statement: If we write $\exp \pi H(\Lambda, \lambda, x) = \sum A_{v, \gamma, u} \Lambda^v \lambda^\gamma x^u$ then clearly $A_{v, \gamma, u} \in R$. Let us write then $\exp \pi H(\Lambda, \lambda, x) = \sum A_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) \lambda^\gamma x^u$ with $A_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) \in R[[\Lambda]]$ and the indices $(\gamma, u) \in M(H) \subset M(\Gamma) \times M(f)$. We will also write \[ pr_0( \exp \pi H(\Lambda, \lambda, x) ) = \sum_{(\gamma, u) \in M_0(\Gamma) \times M_0(f)} J_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma) -w(u)} \lambda^{-\gamma} x^{-u} = \sum_{(\gamma, u) \in M_0(H)} \tilde{J}_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) \tilde \pi^{-w_H(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} x^{-u}. \] The running indices $(\gamma, u)$ in all these sums may be taken in $M_0(H).$
nodes.statement_short: Coefficients of the $\text{pr}_0$-truncation of $\exp \pi H$, indexed by $M_0(H)$.

nodes.name: $J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ is a unit in $\c K$
nodes.statement: Of course, \begin{equation} J_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) = A_{-\gamma, -u}(\Lambda) \tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w(u)} = \tilde{J}_{\gamma,u} \tilde{\pi}^{ w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)+w(u) -w_H(\gamma,u) } \end{equation} for every $(\gamma, u) \in M_0(H)$, and $J_{0,0} = \tilde{J}_{0,0} = A_{0,0} \in 1 + \Lambda \c K$. That is, $J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ is a power series in the variables $ \Lambda$ with coefficients in $R$ and constant term 1. So $J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ is a unit in $\c K$.
nodes.statement_short: $J_{0,0} = \tilde J_{0,0} = A_{0,0} \in 1 + \Lambda\c K$ is a power series with constant term 1, hence invertible.
assumptions: J_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) = A_{-\gamma, -u}(\Lambda) \tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w(u)} = \tilde{J}_{\gamma,u} \tilde{\pi}^{ w_{\Gamma}(\gamma)+w(u) -w_H(\gamma,u) }
conclusions: $J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ is a power series in the variables $ \Lambda$ with coefficients in $R$ and constant term 1.
So $J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ is a unit in $\c K$.

nodes.name: The eigenvector $\eta(\Lambda,\lambda,x)$
nodes.statement: Define \begin{align} \eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) :&= \frac{1}{ J_{00}(\Lambda) } \text{pr}_0 \exp \pi H(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \notag \\ &= 1 + \sum_{\substack{ (\gamma, u) \in M_0(H) \\ (\gamma, u) \not= (0,0)}} \frac{\tilde{J}_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda)}{J_{0,0}(\Lambda)} \tilde \pi^{-w_H(\gamma,u)} \lambda^{-\gamma} x^{-u}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The normalized truncation $\eta = \text{pr}_0(\exp \pi H)/J_{0,0}$, a series with constant term $1$.

nodes.name: Convergence of $J_{0,0}(\Lambda)/J_{0,0}(\Lambda^p)$ on the closed unit polydisk
nodes.statement: In \cite{MR2966711}, it was shown that $J_{0,0}(\Lambda) / J_{0,0}(\Lambda^p)$ and $\tilde{J}_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) / J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ converge on the closed unit polydisk $| \Lambda | \leq 1$ for every $\Lambda$. Equivalently, $J_{0,0}(\Lambda) / J_{0,0}(\Lambda^p)$ and $ \tilde{J}_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) / J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ belong to $\c K_0$. The same holds as well for $ J_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) / J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ using (\ref{E: J's}), since $A_{-\gamma,-u}(\Lambda) \in R[[\Lambda]]$.
nodes.statement_short: The Frobenius ratio and the normalized coefficients converge on $|\Lambda| \le 1$, i.e. lie in $\c K_0$.
assumptions: In \cite{MR2966711}, it was shown that
conclusions: $J_{0,0}(\Lambda) / J_{0,0}(\Lambda^p)$ and $\tilde{J}_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) / J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ converge on the closed unit polydisk $| \Lambda | \leq 1$ for every $\Lambda$.
The same holds as well for $ J_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) / J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ using (\ref{E: J's}), since $A_{-\gamma,-u}(\Lambda) \in R[[\Lambda]]$.

nodes.name: $\eta$ lies in $\c D_0(\c W_0(\c K_0))$
nodes.statement: Since $J_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) = A_{-\gamma, -u} \tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w(u)}$, we have \[ \left| \sum_{\gamma \in M_0(\Gamma)} \frac{J_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda)}{ J_{0,0}(\Lambda)} \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} \right| \leq |\tilde \pi |^{w(u)}, \] and so $\eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \in \c D_0(\c W_0(\c K_0)) \subset \c D( \c W(\c K_0))$.
nodes.statement_short: The normalized coefficients decay like $|\tilde\pi|^{w(u)}$, placing $\eta$ in $\c D_0(\c W_0(\c K_0))$.
assumptions: Since $J_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) = A_{-\gamma, -u} \tilde \pi^{w_\Gamma(\gamma) + w(u)}$
conclusions: and so $\eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \in \c D_0(\c W_0(\c K_0)) \subset \c D( \c W(\c K_0))$.

nodes.name: The unit root function $\c F(\Lambda)$
nodes.statement: Set $\c F(\Lambda) := J_{00}(\Lambda) / J_{00}(\Lambda^p)$.

nodes.name: Frobenius functional equation for $\eta$
nodes.statement: Observe that \[\text{pr}_{M(f)} \circ F_m(\Lambda,\lambda,x) \circ \text{pr}_0 (\exp \pi H(\Lambda^p,\lambda^p,x^p)) = \text{pr}_{M(f)} (\exp \pi H(\Lambda,\lambda,x)) \] so that \begin{align*} \alpha_{1, \Lambda}^*( \eta(\Lambda^p, \lambda^p, x) ) &= \c F(\Lambda) \text{pr}_{M(f)} \left( \frac{\exp \pi H(\Lambda, \lambda, x)}{J_{00}(\Lambda)} \right) \\ &= \c F(\Lambda) \left( \eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) + \tilde \omega (\Lambda, \lambda, x) \right), \end{align*} where each $\lambda^\gamma$ appearing in $\tilde \omega$ lies in $M(\Gamma) \setminus M_0(\Gamma)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\alpha^*_{1,\Lambda}(\eta(\Lambda^p,\lambda^p,x)) = \c F(\Lambda)(\eta + \tilde\omega)$ with $\tilde\omega$ supported off $M_0(\Gamma)$.
assumptions: \text{pr}_{M(f)} \circ F_m(\Lambda,\lambda,x) \circ \text{pr}_0 (\exp \pi H(\Lambda^p,\lambda^p,x^p)) = \text{pr}_{M(f)} (\exp \pi H(\Lambda,\lambda,x))
conclusions: \alpha_{1, \Lambda}^*( \eta(\Lambda^p, \lambda^p, x) ) &= \c F(\Lambda) \text{pr}_{M(f)} \left( \frac{\exp \pi H(\Lambda, \lambda, x)}{J_{00}(\Lambda)} \right)

nodes.name: The iterated function $\c F_m(\Lambda)$
nodes.statement: Iterating this, if we set \[ \c F_m(\Lambda) := \prod_{i=0}^{m-1} \c F(\Lambda^{p^i}), \]

nodes.name: Iterated functional equation for $\eta$
nodes.statement: then we have \begin{equation} \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* \eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x) = \c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\Lambda) \left( \eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) + \omega(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \right), \end{equation} where each $\lambda^\gamma$ appearing in $\omega$ lies in $M(\Gamma) \setminus M_0(\Gamma)$.
nodes.statement_short: Iterating gives $\alpha^*_{ad(\bar t),\Lambda}\eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}},\lambda^{q_{\bar t}},x) = \c F_{ad(\bar t)}(\Lambda)(\eta+\omega)$.
assumptions: \c F_m(\Lambda) := \prod_{i=0}^{m-1} \c F(\Lambda^{p^i})
conclusions: \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* \eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x) = \c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\Lambda) \left( \eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) + \omega(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \right)

nodes.name: The normalized coefficients $Q_{\gamma,u}$
nodes.statement: For notational convenience, set $Q_{\gamma, u} := Q_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) := J_{\gamma, u}(\Lambda) / J_{0,0}(\Lambda)$ so that \[ \eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) = 1 + \sum_{\substack{\gamma \in M_0(\Gamma), u \in M_0(f) \\ (\gamma, u) \not= (0, 0)}} Q_{\gamma, u} \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma) - w(u)} \lambda^{-\gamma} x^{-u}. \] Next, write \[ \Upsilon(\eta) = 1 + \sum_{\substack{\gamma \in M_0(\Gamma), u \in M_0(f) \\ (\gamma, u) \not= (0, 0)}} Q_{\gamma, u} \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_u^*, \]

nodes.name: $\Upsilon(\eta)^\kappa$ lies in $\c S^*(\c W_0(\c K_0))$ and kills $\omega$
nodes.statement: and observe that $\Upsilon(\eta)$ and $1 / \Upsilon(\eta)$ are elements of $\c S_0^*(\c W_0(\c K_0))$. For $\kappa \in \bb Z_p$, we compute \begin{align*} (\Upsilon(\eta))^\kappa &= \sum_{l=0}^\infty \binom{\kappa}{l}(\sum Q_{\gamma, u} \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma)} \lambda^{-\gamma} e_u^*)^l \\ &= \sum_{l=0}^\kappa \binom{\kappa}{l} \sum_{\substack{\gamma_1, \ldots, \gamma_l \in M_0(\Gamma) \\ u_1, \ldots, u_l \in M_0(f) \\ (\gamma_j, u_j) \not= (0, 0) \text{ for every j}} } Q_{\gamma_1, u_1} \cdots Q_{\gamma_l, u_l} \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma_1) - \cdots - w_\Gamma(\gamma_l)} \lambda^{-(\gamma_1 + \cdots + \gamma_l)} e_{u_1}^* \cdots e_{u_l}^* \\ &= \sum_{l = 0}^\infty \binom{\kappa}{l} \sum_{\substack{\gamma_1, \ldots, \gamma_l \in M_0(\Gamma) \\ u_1, \ldots, u_l \in M_0(f) \\ (\gamma_j, u_j) \not= (0, 0) \text{ for every j}} } \widetilde{Q}_{\gamma, u} \cdot \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma_1 + \cdots + \gamma_l)} \lambda^{-(\gamma_1 + \cdots + \gamma_l)} e_{u_1}^* \cdots e_{u_l}^* \end{align*} where \[ \widetilde{Q}_{\gamma, u} := Q_{\gamma_1, u_1} \cdots Q_{\gamma_l, u_l} \tilde \pi^{-w_\Gamma(\gamma_1) - \cdots - w_\Gamma(\gamma_l) + w_\Gamma(\gamma_1 + \cdots + \gamma_l)}. \] Hence, $(\Upsilon(\eta))^\kappa \in \c S^*(\c W_0(\c K_0))$. As every $\lambda^\gamma$ appearing in $\Upsilon(\omega)$ (from equation (\ref{E: first formula})) satisfies $\gamma \in M(\Gamma) \setminus M_0(\Gamma)$, it follows that the same is true for $( \Upsilon(\omega) / \Upsilon(\eta) )^r$ for any $r \in \bb Z_{\geq 1}$. Hence, \[ \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \left(1 + \frac{\Upsilon(\omega)}{\Upsilon(\eta) } \right)^\kappa = 1. \]
nodes.statement_short: The binomial expansion of $\Upsilon(\eta)^\kappa$ converges in $\c S^*(\c W_0(\c K_0))$, and the $\omega$-correction is annihilated by $\text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)}$.
assumptions: For $\kappa \in \bb Z_p$, we compute
conclusions: Hence, $(\Upsilon(\eta))^\kappa \in \c S^*(\c W_0(\c K_0))$.
\text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \left(1 + \frac{\Upsilon(\omega)}{\Upsilon(\eta) } \right)^\kappa = 1.

nodes.name: Proof of the unit root formula, completing the Main Theorem
nodes.statement: We may now finish the proof of Theorem \ref{T: Main Thm}. For convenience, write $\eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) = 1 + h(\Lambda, \lambda, x)$ so that $\Upsilon(\eta)^\kappa = (1 + \Upsilon(h))^\kappa = \sum_{l=0}^\infty \binom{\kappa}{l} \Upsilon(h)^l$. Observe that \begin{align*} \beta_{\kappa, \bar t, \Lambda}^* \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda, x))^\kappa &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \circ [\alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^*]_\kappa \circ \Phi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)} \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda, x))^\kappa \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \circ [\alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^*]_\kappa \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x))^\kappa \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \circ [\alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^*]_\kappa \sum_{l=0}^\infty \binom{\kappa}{l} \Upsilon \left( h(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x) \right)^l \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \sum_{l=0}^\infty \binom{\kappa}{l} \left(\Upsilon \circ \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* \cdot 1 \right)^{\kappa - l} \left(\Upsilon \circ \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* h(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x) \right)^l \qquad \text{by definition of $ [\alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^*]_\kappa$} \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \> \left( \Upsilon \circ \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* \cdot 1 + \Upsilon \circ \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* h(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x) \right)^\kappa \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \> \left( \Upsilon \circ \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* \eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x) \right)^\kappa \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \> \c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\Lambda)^\kappa \left( \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) + \Upsilon(\omega(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \right)^\kappa \qquad \text{by } (\ref{E: first formula}) \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \> \c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\Lambda)^\kappa \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x))^\kappa \left( 1 + \frac{\Upsilon(\omega(\Lambda, \lambda, x))}{\Upsilon( \eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x))} \right)^\kappa \\ &= \c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\Lambda)^\kappa \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x))^\kappa. \end{align*} Finally, we may specialize this equality taking $\Lambda$ at the Teichm\"uller unit coefficients of $\hat G(\hat t, \lambda, x)$: \[ \Lambda_u = \hat t_u \qquad \text{and} \qquad \Lambda_{\gamma, v} = \hat A(\gamma, v) \qquad \text{for all $u$ and $\gamma, v$ in the support of $H$}, \] and setting \[ \eta_{\text{sp}}(\lambda, x) := \left( \eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \text{ specialized at $\Lambda_u = \hat t_u$ and $\Lambda_{\gamma, v} = \hat A(\gamma, v)$} \right), \] then we see that \begin{equation} \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^* \Upsilon(\eta_{\text{sp}}(\lambda, x))^\kappa = \c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\hat t)^\kappa \Upsilon(\eta_{\text{sp}}(\lambda, x))^\kappa \end{equation} This demonstrates that $\c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\hat t)^\kappa$ is the unique unit root of $L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}}$ by (\ref{E: L0 and dual}), which, together with Theorem \ref{T: unique unit}, completes the proof of Theorem \ref{T: Main Thm}.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\Upsilon(\eta)^\kappa$ is an eigenvector of $\beta^*_{\kappa,\bar t,\Lambda}$ with eigenvalue $\c F_{ad(\bar t)}(\Lambda)^\kappa$, then specialize $\Lambda$ at Teichm\"uller coefficients and combine with the duality and uniqueness theorems.

nodes.name: Set up the binomial expansion of $\Upsilon(\eta)^\kappa$
nodes.statement: For convenience, write $\eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) = 1 + h(\Lambda, \lambda, x)$ so that $\Upsilon(\eta)^\kappa = (1 + \Upsilon(h))^\kappa = \sum_{l=0}^\infty \binom{\kappa}{l} \Upsilon(h)^l$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $\eta = 1+h$ so that $\Upsilon(\eta)^\kappa$ is the binomial series in $\Upsilon(h)$.

nodes.name: Compute $\beta^*_{\kappa,\bar t,\Lambda}$ on $\Upsilon(\eta)^\kappa$
nodes.statement: Observe that \begin{align*} \beta_{\kappa, \bar t, \Lambda}^* \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda, x))^\kappa &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \circ [\alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^*]_\kappa \circ \Phi_\lambda^{a d(\bar t)} \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda, x))^\kappa \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \circ [\alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^*]_\kappa \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x))^\kappa \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \circ [\alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^*]_\kappa \sum_{l=0}^\infty \binom{\kappa}{l} \Upsilon \left( h(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x) \right)^l \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \sum_{l=0}^\infty \binom{\kappa}{l} \left(\Upsilon \circ \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* \cdot 1 \right)^{\kappa - l} \left(\Upsilon \circ \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* h(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x) \right)^l \qquad \text{by definition of $ [\alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^*]_\kappa$} \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \> \left( \Upsilon \circ \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* \cdot 1 + \Upsilon \circ \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* h(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x) \right)^\kappa \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \> \left( \Upsilon \circ \alpha_{a d(\bar t), \Lambda}^* \eta(\Lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, \lambda^{q_{\bar t}}, x) \right)^\kappa \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \> \c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\Lambda)^\kappa \left( \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) + \Upsilon(\omega(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \right)^\kappa \qquad \text{by } (\ref{E: first formula}) \\ &= \text{pr}_{M(\Gamma)} \> \c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\Lambda)^\kappa \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x))^\kappa \left( 1 + \frac{\Upsilon(\omega(\Lambda, \lambda, x))}{\Upsilon( \eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x))} \right)^\kappa \\ &= \c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\Lambda)^\kappa \Upsilon(\eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x))^\kappa. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain the definition of $[\alpha^*]_\kappa$, the iterated functional equation, and the vanishing of the $\omega$-correction to get the eigenvector identity.

nodes.name: Specialize $\Lambda$ at the Teichm\"uller coefficients
nodes.statement: Finally, we may specialize this equality taking $\Lambda$ at the Teichm\"uller unit coefficients of $\hat G(\hat t, \lambda, x)$: \[ \Lambda_u = \hat t_u \qquad \text{and} \qquad \Lambda_{\gamma, v} = \hat A(\gamma, v) \qquad \text{for all $u$ and $\gamma, v$ in the support of $H$}, \] and setting \[ \eta_{\text{sp}}(\lambda, x) := \left( \eta(\Lambda, \lambda, x) \text{ specialized at $\Lambda_u = \hat t_u$ and $\Lambda_{\gamma, v} = \hat A(\gamma, v)$} \right), \] then we see that \begin{equation} \beta_{\kappa, \bar t}^* \Upsilon(\eta_{\text{sp}}(\lambda, x))^\kappa = \c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\hat t)^\kappa \Upsilon(\eta_{\text{sp}}(\lambda, x))^\kappa \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Set $\Lambda_u = \hat t_u$, $\Lambda_{\gamma,v} = \hat A(\gamma,v)$ to obtain the specialized eigenvalue equation for $\beta^*_{\kappa,\bar t}$.

nodes.name: Conclude the Main Theorem
nodes.statement: This demonstrates that $\c F_{a d(\bar t)}(\hat t)^\kappa$ is the unique unit root of $L^{(0)}(\kappa, \bar t, T)^{(-1)^{s+1}}$ by (\ref{E: L0 and dual}), which, together with Theorem \ref{T: unique unit}, completes the proof of Theorem \ref{T: Main Thm}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the duality identity for $L^{(0)}$ with the uniqueness theorem to identify the unit root and finish the proof.
